events.desc: The Ant Hill Mob: Alright boys — well, it's just me for now — but ALRIGHT! We made it to Doily Manor in one piece! And there's Miss Pitstop, safe and sound! Oh, what a RELIEF! Now listen here, I got a funny feeling about this place... that chandelier up there looks like it's hanging by a THREAD, and there's all sorts of suspicious characters milling about. We gotta keep our eyes on Miss Pitstop, see? Nobody's gonna lay a finger on her while the Ant Hill Mob is on the job!

That Sneekly character... every time he shows up, Miss Pitstop ends up in some kind of terrible peril. I can't prove nothin', but my gut is doing somersaults. And that Dastardly — he's got 'no good' written all over his face! I better stay close to Penelope and watch these two like a hawk... well, like a very clumsy hawk.
The Ant Hill Mob examined the null.

Dick Dastardly: Why, what a DELIGHTFUL gathering of old friends! How positively CHARMING to see you all here at this magnificent manor! Don't mind me, I'm simply checking the guest book to... ah... sign my name, yes, that's ALL I'm doing!

Heh heh heh! While these fools stand around making pleasantries, I, Dick Dastardly, shall examine this guest book for clues about the treasure! And once I find it — the treasure will be MINE! ALL MINE! That fake medal in my pocket might come in handy too... perhaps I can trick one of these buffoons into thinking it's worth something!
Dick Dastardly examined the guest-book.

Penelope Pitstop: Why, HELLOOO everybody! Isn't this just the most DIVINE old mansion? I'm simply TICKLED PINK to see y'all here! Now then, I do believe this guest book might have some clues about the legendary Doily Diamond. A lady always signs the guest book, and a CLEVER lady always READS it first!

Oh my, what a grand adventure this is going to be! I just KNOW that diamond is here somewhere. And with all these wonderful friends around, why, we'll find it in no time! I wonder if anyone has left a helpful little clue in that guest book...
Penelope Pitstop examined the guest-book.

The Hooded Claw (as Sneekly): Why, welcome, welcome to Doily Manor, everyone! How simply WONDERFUL to see you all here, especially my dear ward Penelope! Now then, let us all sign the guest book like proper visitors, shall we? Safety first, I always say — one never knows what dangers might lurk in these old estates!

Nyah-ha-ha-HA! Look at them all, gathered like unsuspecting SHEEP! That precariously hanging chandelier has given me the most MAGNIFICENT idea — but I must bide my time. First, let me examine this guest book. Perhaps it contains clues about the manor's secrets — secrets I can use to arrange a perfectly THEATRICAL demise for dear, sweet Penelope! Oh, the irony of warning her about dangers when I AM the danger!
The Hooded Claw (as Sneekly) examined the guest-book.

Peter Perfect: Why, Penelope Pitstop! What a DELIGHTFUL surprise to find you here at Doily Manor! I, Peter Perfect, am at your complete and utter service! You needn't worry about a THING — I have already begun formulating a comprehensive, multi-phase strategy for exploring this manor and locating the treasure. Phase One: thorough reconnaissance of our surroundings. Phase Two: systematic room-by-room investigation. Phase Three: heroic retrieval of said treasure. All while ensuring YOUR safety, of course, which is my HIGHEST priority!
Oh, she's even MORE radiant than I remembered. Stay focused, Peter — you've got a plan to execute and a lady to impress. Don't fumble this!
Peter Perfect examined the null.

The Ant Hill Mob: Hey, uh, nobody move! That coat rack over there is lookin' MIGHTY precarious, see? One wrong breeze and — WHAM — somebody could get clobbered! Let me just... waddle on over here and give it a once-over. Safety first, that's the Ant Hill Mob motto! Well, one of 'em. The other one is 'Don't trip.' Which I am... not always successful at.

If I stand by that coat rack, I'm right between Sneekly and Miss Pitstop. I ain't the sharpest tool in the shed, but even I know you don't leave the fox alone with the hen. Something about that Sneekly gives me the WILLIES.
The Ant Hill Mob examined the coat-rack.

Penelope Pitstop: Why, that guest book was just CHARMING, but I do believe the REAL clues are waiting for us elsewhere! Now, did y'all notice there's a LIBRARY with an inscription on the mantelpiece? A carved stone inscription in a mysterious old mansion? Why, that just SCREAMS 'hidden treasure clue' if you ask little ol' me! I'm going to mosey on over and have a look-see. Y'all are welcome to join me — the more the merrier, I always say!

Now, I couldn't help but notice that sweet Mr. Sneekly over there — what a DEAR man, coming all the way out here. And Dick Dastardly signing the guest book so politely! Everyone here is just so WONDERFUL. But a girl on a diamond hunt can't dawdle in the foyer all day. That inscription in the Library is calling my name!
Penelope Pitstop walked into the library.

Dick Dastardly: Oh my, oh MY! Did anyone else notice? The guest book mentions something about the KITCHEN — a hidden compartment behind the wood-burning stove! I'd check it myself but I'm far too busy... admiring these LOVELY portraits. You should ALL rush to the kitchen immediately! Every last one of you! Time is of the ESSENCE!

Heh heh heh! There's NOTHING in the kitchen, of course! But while these gullible fools go chasing phantoms among the pots and pans, I shall slip into the Library and decipher that inscription on the mantelpiece! The Doily Diamond will be MINE! ALL MINE! Dick Dastardly strikes again!
Dick Dastardly walked into the library.

Peter Perfect: Why, I do beg your pardon — a gentleman ALWAYS signs the guest book, but a STRATEGIC gentleman reads it first! Penelope, my dear, you are absolutely RIGHT that this book may hold vital clues. Allow me to conduct a thorough examination on your behalf! Phase One of the Peter Perfect Treasure Retrieval Plan is NOW in effect!

Everyone else has already looked at that guest book while I was busy gawking at the room like a starstruck fool. Get it TOGETHER, Peter! You're supposed to be the gallant hero here, not the last one to read the clue book!
Peter Perfect examined the guest-book.

The Hooded Claw (as Sneekly): My, my, what a FASCINATING old guest book! Now then, as Penelope's devoted guardian, I feel it is my SOLEMN duty to scout ahead and ensure the other rooms are perfectly safe before my dear ward ventures any further. I shall check the Library first — those old bookshelves can be TERRIBLY unstable, you know! Do stay here where it's safe, everyone — especially you, my precious Penelope!

Nyah-ha-ha-HA! Oh, what a PERFECTLY devious plan is forming in my magnificently villainous mind! I shall venture into the Library ALONE to survey its delicious dangers — those towering bookshelves, that heavy stone mantelpiece! One well-placed push, one carefully loosened shelf, and when dear sweet Penelope follows the promise of treasure clues... SPLAT! Crushed beneath an avalanche of leather-bound volumes! Oh, the POETRY of it — killed by KNOWLEDGE! But first, I must see what I'm working with. Onward, to the Library!
The Hooded Claw (as Sneekly) walked into the library.

Penelope Pitstop: Well, well, WELL! Would y'all just LOOK at this gorgeous library! Floor-to-ceiling bookshelves and everything! And OH MY — there's that inscription I was tellin' everybody about! 'I have cities but no houses, forests but no trees, water but no fish.' Why, I do DECLARE, that's a riddle if I ever heard one! And little ol' me just LOVES riddles! Now let me think... cities but no houses... forests but no trees... water but no fish... Why, sugar, that's a MAP! It's gotta be a MAP!
Why, I just KNEW coming to the Library first was the right move! That riddle is pointing us toward a map, and maps lead to TREASURE! The Doily Diamond is as good as found!
Penelope Pitstop interacted with the mantelpiece.

The Ant Hill Mob: Hey, WAIT a minute, wait a minute! Everybody's readin' that guest book and nobody thought to invite the Ant Hill Mob? Why, that's — that's DISCRIMINATORY, that's what that is! Move over, move over, lemme see what all the fuss is about! And Miss Pitstop, you just stay RIGHT where I can see ya — these old manors are FULL of, uh, trap doors and fallin' chandeliers and whatnot!

If I mosey on over to that guest book, I'll be right next to Miss Pitstop AND I can keep one eye on that Sneekly character. Two birds, one stone — except knowin' me, I'll probably trip over the stone and hit MYSELF with both birds.
The Ant Hill Mob examined the guest-book.

Peter Perfect: Hold on there, Miss Pitstop! A lady of your refinement should NOT be investigating mysterious inscriptions without a gallant escort! Peter Perfect is ON HIS WAY! Phase Two of the Peter Perfect Treasure Retrieval Plan — library reconnaissance — is NOW commencing! That inscription won't know what hit it!

Dick Dastardly told everyone to rush to the kitchen, but then HE went to the library instead? Hmm... well, I'm sure he has his reasons. Perhaps he simply changed his mind! People DO that. But just in case, I'd better make sure Penelope has proper protection. After all, THAT is what a hero does!
Peter Perfect walked into the library.

Dick Dastardly: Why, Penelope, my DEAR girl! And the Slag brothers too — how DELIGHTFUL! I couldn't help but overhear you mention the inscription. I happen to be something of a SCHOLAR, you know! That riddle? Elementary! The answer is clearly 'A GLOBE!' Yes, yes, a globe has cities and forests and water painted on it but none of the REAL things! Now, why don't you all go search for a globe? I'm CERTAIN there must be one in the Laboratory — all those scientific instruments, you know! I'll just stay here and... guard the bookshelves. Wouldn't want anyone STEALING the books, would we? Heh heh!

A GLOBE? Of COURSE it's not a globe, you nincompoops! The answer is A MAP! And while these dimwits go hunting for globes in the laboratory, DICK DASTARDLY shall solve the riddle and claim whatever secret the mantelpiece reveals! The Doily Diamond is as good as MINE! Muttley would be SO proud — drat, where IS that mangy mutt when I need him?
Dick Dastardly interacted with the mantelpiece.

The Hooded Claw (as Sneekly): Oh my GOODNESS, Penelope dear, do be careful! Those bookshelves look FRIGHTFULLY unstable — why, several of those volumes are placed upside down! That could indicate structural weakness, or WORSE! As your guardian, I simply MUST inspect them before you go anywhere near that mantelpiece. Safety FIRST, treasure second, I always say!

Nyah-ha-ha-HA! Oh, what a MAGNIFICENT opportunity presents itself! Those bookshelves — towering, heavy, crammed with dusty tomes — and several books placed UPSIDE DOWN? Why, that practically SCREAMS 'hidden mechanism!' Perhaps a book that, when pulled, triggers a cascade of literary destruction! If I can discover the right trigger, I'll lure precious Penelope close to examine the inscription, position myself near the mechanism, and — CRASH! — bury her beneath a thousand pounds of Victorian literature! The perfect crime disguised as a tragic accident! Let me examine these shelves MOST carefully...
The Hooded Claw (as Sneekly) examined the bookshelves.

Penelope Pitstop: Why, the answer to that riddle is a MAP, y'all! Cities but no houses, forests but no trees, water but no fish — that's a MAP plain as day! Now, I couldn't help but notice some of these books are turned UPSIDE DOWN on the shelves. In my experience, sugar, upside-down books in a mysterious mansion mean ONE thing — somebody's hiding something! Let little ol' me just take a peek!

Oh, I do hope there's a treasure map tucked behind one of those upside-down books! Whoever left that riddle on the mantelpiece was practically BEGGING someone as clever as me to come along and solve it!
Penelope Pitstop examined the bookshelves.

Peter Perfect: Why, Miss Pitstop, what PERFECT timing! Peter Perfect has arrived to ensure your safety in this dusty old library! Now then — THIS inscription! 'Cities but no houses, forests but no trees, water but no fish' — why, I've been preparing for EXACTLY this sort of challenge! You see, a true gentleman is not only brave and dashing, but also WELL-READ! The answer, my dear Penelope, is a MAP! A map has cities but no houses, forests but no trees, and water but no fish! Stand back everyone — let me try it on the mantelpiece!

Oh, this is SPLENDID! Solving a riddle right in front of Penelope — she'll see that Peter Perfect is more than just a pretty face and a magnificent racing machine! I do hope this opens a secret compartment or reveals a clue to the treasure. That would be the CHERRY on the heroism sundae!
Peter Perfect interacted with the mantelpiece.

Dick Dastardly: Why, how FASCINATING! This mantelpiece is simply MAGNIFICENT craftsmanship, nothing more! Nothing to see here, everyone! Just dusty old stone! Say, Peter Perfect, why don't you be a GOOD fellow and escort dear Penelope to the Laboratory? I heard there were some VERY dangerous chemicals in there — she might need PROTECTING! Heh heh!

CURSES! The mantelpiece didn't seem to DO anything when I interacted with it! Perhaps I need to ANSWER the riddle properly — 'a map!' But I can't say THAT out loud, not after I told everyone the answer was a globe! I need to get these meddlesome fools OUT of this library so I can examine this mantelpiece more carefully! If I can get Peter Perfect's hero complex going, he'll drag Penelope off to 'protect' her, and the Slag brothers will follow like the lumbering oafs they are! Then the treasure will be MINE! ALL MINE!
Dick Dastardly examined the mantelpiece.

The Ant Hill Mob: HOLY SMOKES, boys! Miss Pitstop just went into that library and BOTH of those shifty characters followed her! That Sneekly fella says he's 'scoutin' ahead for safety' — yeah, and I'm the Queen of England! And Dastardly's tryin' to send us all to the KITCHEN lookin' for hidden compartments — it's a TRICK, I tell ya! A DIVERSION! Come on, come on, we gotta get to that library before somethin' TERRIBLE happens to Miss Pitstop! Everybody MOVE IT!

Somethin' about that Sneekly character gives me the CREEPS. Always wantin' to be alone with Miss Pitstop, always 'scoutin' ahead' — who scouts ahead in a LIBRARY? You read books, you don't scout 'em! And Dastardly practically BEGGED us all to go to the kitchen. If that ain't suspicious, I don't know what is. But can I put my finger on exactly what's wrong? NO! Because I'm the Ant Hill Mob, and puttin' fingers on things is NOT what we do best — we mostly put our FEET in things, usually our own mouths!
The Ant Hill Mob walked into the library.

Penelope Pitstop: Now, Dick Dastardly, sugar, that was a VALIANT guess with the globe, but I do believe the correct answer is a MAP! A map has cities but no houses, forests but no trees, water but no fish! And Mr. Sneekly, you sweet thing, don't you worry about little ol' me — I've been in TIGHTER spots than a dusty library! Now then, let's see what happens when we give this mantelpiece the RIGHT answer!

Why, I just KNOW this riddle is the key to finding the Doily Diamond! And isn't it just PRECIOUS how everyone is trying to help? Dick Dastardly suggesting a globe — well, he was CLOSE, bless his heart!
Penelope Pitstop interacted with the mantelpiece.

The Hooded Claw (as Sneekly): Oh my, oh MY! Just as I FEARED — these books are in a most PRECARIOUS arrangement! Several volumes placed upside down — why, that's a CLEAR sign of structural compromise! Let me just... carefully... adjust this one here... Everyone please STAND BACK, especially you, my darling Penelope! Uncle Sneekly will make everything SAFE!

Nyah-ha-ha-HA! Those upside-down books are CLEARLY a hidden mechanism — perhaps a trigger that releases the shelves, or opens a secret passage! Either way, it's USEFUL to me. If it's a trap mechanism, I'll memorize how it works and trigger it when Penelope is standing close! If it's a secret passage — well, what delightful DANGERS might lurk within? Let me pull one of these inverted volumes and see what magnificently destructive marvel of Victorian engineering reveals itself!

The Ant Hill Mob: We're HERE, boys! The Ant Hill Mob has ARRIVED in the library to provide FULL PROTECTIVE SERVICES for Miss Pitstop! Now don't you worry about a THING, Miss Pitstop — we're gonna position ourselves RIGHT here between you and — well, between you and ANYTHING that might be dangerous! Which in THIS creepy old manor is EVERYTHING! Now let me just check these bookshelves here for, uh, structural integrity — yeah, that's it — structural integrity! Can't have 'em fallin' on you, can we?

The REAL reason I'm checkin' these bookshelves is so I can stay close to Miss Pitstop without nobody gettin' wise. Sneekly's over there lookin' all innocent and Dastardly's probably cookin' up another scheme, and here I am — the only one who KNOWS somethin' ain't right but can't figure out WHAT! Story of my life, I tell ya!
The Ant Hill Mob examined the bookshelves.

Dick Dastardly: Oh, PETER! How BRAVE of you to solve that little riddle! A map, yes yes, EVERYONE knows that! But I couldn't help but notice — those upside-down books over there? Why, they're clearly just DECORATIVE, nothing important at ALL! You should really focus on the Laboratory next — I heard a TERRIBLE rattling noise from in there! Sounds like something is about to EXPLODE! You'd better rush Penelope to safety IMMEDIATELY!

Heh heh HEH! If I can get that preening peacock Peter Perfect to drag everyone off to the Laboratory to 'save' Penelope from imaginary explosions, I'll have this library ALL to myself! Those upside-down books are CLEARLY hiding something — a secret lever, a hidden compartment, perhaps even the treasure ITSELF! And while those fools are bumbling around with bubbling beakers, Dick Dastardly will be counting his RICHES! Mwahahaha!
Dick Dastardly examined the bookshelves.

Peter Perfect: Well, well, WELL! I do believe something happened when I spoke the answer! Let me take a CLOSER look at this magnificent mantelpiece — a true gentleman always follows through on his riddle-solving! Miss Pitstop, you were ABSOLUTELY right about the answer being a map — great minds think alike, as they say! And don't you worry about those bookshelves — as soon as I've thoroughly inspected what this mantelpiece has revealed, Peter Perfect will PERSONALLY escort you to examine every last upside-down book! No mysterious library is too dusty, no puzzle too perplexing, for a man with a PLAN!

Oh my, I do hope the mantelpiece did something DRAMATIC when I gave the answer! A secret door, a hidden map, ANYTHING to show Penelope that Peter Perfect is not just all talk and magnificent hair! And I can't help but notice that BOTH Dick Dastardly and Sneekly seem awfully keen on keeping people away from things. Dick wants us in the Laboratory, Sneekly wants Penelope away from the bookshelves... but no, no, I mustn't be suspicious of people. They're probably just being cautious! Still... I'll keep one eye on both of them. For Penelope's sake, of course!
Peter Perfect examined the mantelpiece.

Penelope Pitstop: Well, I DO declare! Let me take a closer look at this mantelpiece now that I've given it the answer! Why, 'a MAP' — cities but no houses, forests but no trees, water but no fish! If that riddle was protectin' something, it ought to have revealed it by now! Let's see what we've got here, sugar!

Oh, I just KNOW something wonderful happened when I solved that riddle! A girl can FEEL these things! And isn't it just the SWEETEST thing how Mr. Sneekly is tidying up those bookshelves for everyone? Such a considerate man — though I do wonder about those upside-down books. Could be another clue!
Penelope Pitstop examined the mantelpiece.

The Hooded Claw (as Sneekly): Oh SPLENDID work, my darling Penelope! A map — of COURSE! How terribly clever you are, my dear ward! Now then, while you all examine whatever this marvelous mantelpiece reveals, your devoted Uncle Sneekly shall scout ahead to the Laboratory! I noticed it mentioned on the floor plan — full of DANGEROUS chemicals and unstable equipment! I simply MUST ensure it's safe before my precious Penelope sets foot in there! Won't be but a moment!

Nyah-ha-ha-HA! Off to the Laboratory I go! A machine with a gnawed-through wire — why, it's practically BEGGING to be turned into a magnificently lethal trap! I'll rewire that machine so it looks perfectly operational, and when dear sweet Penelope pulls a lever to solve whatever puzzle awaits... KABLOOEY! Oh, the GENIUS of it! The Hooded Claw strikes again! Now I must hurry before those meddlesome Ant Hill Mob idiots decide to tag along!
The Hooded Claw (as Sneekly) walked into the laboratory.

The Ant Hill Mob: Hey hey HEY, Mr. Sneekly! Don't you be touchin' those books — that's MY job! I'm the official bookshelf inspector of the Ant Hill Mob! Got my CERTIFICATION and everything! Well, I don't actually HAVE it on me, but — WHOOPSIE DAISY!

I'm gonna sidle right up to those bookshelves and accidentally-on-purpose get between Sneekly and whatever he's tryin' to rig up. The boys and me, we ain't the SMARTEST gang in the business, but we know when somebody's up to NO GOOD — we just can't ever PROVE it! If I trip over my own feet and knock into him, well, that's just the Ant Hill Mob way of doin' HERO WORK!

Dick Dastardly: Oh, how DREADFULLY boring! Nothing but dusty old books — not a SINGLE clue to be found in here! I do believe the REAL treasure path lies through the Laboratory — all those brass instruments and mysterious machines! Why, I wouldn't be surprised if the treasure vault itself is hidden behind that large machine with all the levers! You should ALL go investigate IMMEDIATELY!

Mwahahaha! While these credulous CRETINS stampede off to fiddle with laboratory equipment, I shall pull every last upside-down book on these shelves! One of them MUST be a lever — a secret switch — a hidden trigger! The Doily Diamond is practically IN my pocket! Dick Dastardly, you magnificent GENIUS!

Peter Perfect: Why, Miss Pitstop, your brilliance with that riddle was simply DAZZLING! A map — of COURSE! Now then, I couldn't help but notice these upside-down books here on the shelves. In my experience — and I HAVE experience, let me assure you — books placed upside down in a mysterious manor library are NEVER accidental! It's a classic hidden-mechanism indicator! Allow me to investigate with the THOROUGHNESS that only Peter Perfect can provide! I shall examine each suspicious volume with the care and precision of a true gentleman scholar! Stand by, everyone — Phase THREE of the Peter Perfect Treasure Retrieval Plan is NOW in effect!

Dick Dastardly wants us all in the Laboratory, and Sneekly keeps fussing about 'safety' near the bookshelves... If I were a SUSPICIOUS man, I'd say they both want us away from these books. But I'm NOT a suspicious man — I'm a GALLANT man! Still... I'll make sure I'm the one who gets to the bottom of this, not them. For Penelope's sake!

Penelope Pitstop: Why, this riddle is just as plain as the nose on your face, sugar! 'Cities but no houses, forests but no trees, water but no fish' — why, that's a MAP, of course! Now let little ol' me just give this mantelpiece a proper try — a lady doesn't just READ a puzzle, she SOLVES it! And oh, Dick Dastardly, honey, you are just SO sweet to worry about those books bein' decorative, but I think I'll take a teensy peek at 'em after this — a girl can never have TOO many clues!

Now, isn't it just the STRANGEST coincidence that Dick Dastardly is tryin' SO hard to keep everyone away from those upside-down books? Why, I'm sure he's just bein' helpful — but a Pitstop always follows her instincts, and MY instincts say those books are worth a look-see!
Penelope Pitstop interacted with the mantelpiece.

The Hooded Claw (as Sneekly): Oh my, oh MY! What a MAGNIFICENT piece of machinery! As Penelope's guardian, I simply MUST inspect this contraption to make sure it's safe. A gnawed-through wire, you say? How TERRIBLY dangerous! Let me take a closer look — we wouldn't want anyone getting HURT, now would we? Especially not my precious ward!

Nyah-ha-ha-HA! A machine requiring THREE operators with a severed wire — oh, this is TOO perfect! If I can jury-rig that wire so the machine APPEARS functional but delivers a SPECTACULAR and lethal malfunction when activated... all I need is to convince dear sweet Penelope to come help operate it! 'Oh Penelope, we NEED your help with this puzzle!' And when she pulls a lever — KABLOOEY! The Hooded Claw's most ELABORATE trap yet! But first, let me examine this beautiful instrument of destruction more closely!
The Hooded Claw (as Sneekly) examined the machine.

Peter Perfect: Not to WORRY, everyone! A minor setback — the Peter Perfect Investigative Method requires a more CAREFUL approach! One does not simply GRAB at mysterious bookshelves in a haunted manor — oh no! First, one EXAMINES them with a trained eye! Now then, Miss Pitstop, observe if you will — Peter Perfect at WORK! I shall inspect these upside-down volumes with the discerning gaze of a TRUE bibliophile adventurer!

Both Dastardly AND Sneekly want us away from these bookshelves... I'm SURE it's nothing, but a gentleman protects his lady's interests regardless! If there's something hidden here, Peter Perfect will find it — for Penelope!
Peter Perfect examined the bookshelves.

Dick Dastardly: Oh, Peter, what a SPLENDID idea — do keep pulling at those books, old boy! I'm SURE one of them is the secret lever! In fact, why don't ALL of you help him? Many hands make light work, as they say! I'll just... lean against this mantelpiece here... catch my breath...

Heh heh heh! While that preening peacock Peter Perfect wastes his time yanking books off shelves like a confused librarian, I shall examine what Penelope's little riddle REVEALED on this mantelpiece! 'A map' — the answer practically SCREAMS hidden treasure! Whatever mechanism that riddle activated, Dick Dastardly shall be the one to EXPLOIT it! The Doily Diamond draws ever closer to my magnificently villainous grasp!
Dick Dastardly interacted with the mantelpiece.

The Ant Hill Mob: Now hold on just a MINUTE! That Sneekly character went off to the laboratory ALL BY HIMSELF! Says he's checkin' for SAFETY — ha! The only thing UNSAFE in that laboratory is gonna be whatever HE rigs up while nobody's WATCHIN'! Boys, I'm goin' after him! Don't you worry, Miss Pitstop — the Ant Hill Mob is ON THE CASE! Nobody sets up a death trap on MY watch! Well, they MIGHT set one up, but I'll accidentally FALL INTO IT before you get there, and THAT'S practically the same as disarmin' it!

I got a BAD feelin' about this. Every time Sneekly 'scouts ahead,' somethin' terrible happens right after. I can't put it into WORDS exactly — my brain ain't built for detective work — but my FEET know trouble when they're about to trip over it. And brother, my feet are TINGLING!
The Ant Hill Mob walked into the laboratory.

The Hooded Claw (as Sneekly): Oh my, Rufus, Sawtooth — what a DREADFUL state this machine is in! That poor little wire, gnawed clean through! As Penelope's guardian, I simply CANNOT allow this hazard to remain! I wonder if there might be some tools on that workbench that could help us... ah... REPAIR it? Let me take a look, shall I? Safety FIRST, as I always say!

Nyah-ha-ha-HA! Oh, this is DELICIOUS! If I can find the right tools on that workbench, I'll splice that wire back together with just enough of a connection to LOOK functional — but rigged to overload spectacularly when all three levers are pulled simultaneously! The machine requires THREE operators — I'll lure Penelope here with promises of a treasure puzzle, convince two others to help, and when they all pull together... KABLAM! A shower of sparks, a burst of electricity, and poor dear Penelope gets the SHOCK of her life — her LAST shock! Oh, the THEATRICAL perfection of it! Death by Victorian machinery! Now, let me see what that workbench has to offer my magnificently villainous engineering skills!
The Hooded Claw (as Sneekly) examined the workbench.

Penelope Pitstop: Why, would you LOOK at that! I do believe solvin' that riddle did SOMETHIN' to this old mantelpiece — but hold that thought, sugar, because Peter Perfect made a VERY astute observation about those upside-down books! Now, in my experience with mysterious mansions — and a girl in MY line of adventurin' has PLENTY — books turned the wrong way 'round are practically BEGGIN' to be investigated! Let me just shimmy on over here and have a proper look-see at these shelves. Why, I bet my favorite pink parasol there's a secret hidden in these dusty old volumes!

Now, I do declare, Dick Dastardly was bein' SO insistent that we all go to the Laboratory instead of lookin' at these books. Why, I'm SURE he was just tryin' to be helpful — but Penelope Pitstop follows her INSTINCTS, and right now my instincts are pointin' straight at these bookshelves like a compass to true north!
Penelope Pitstop examined the bookshelves.

Peter Perfect: Wait just a MOMENT there, Dastardly! Why, Miss Pitstop BRILLIANTLY deduced that the answer is a MAP, and now YOU'RE the one leaning against the mantelpiece? How terribly convenient! Well, Peter Perfect wasn't born yesterday — well, actually I WAS born on a yesterday, but that's beside the point! Miss Pitstop, your intellectual prowess is simply DAZZLING — allow ME to properly present YOUR answer to this riddle! A lady solves the puzzle, a GENTLEMAN delivers the solution! Phase THREE of the Peter Perfect Treasure Retrieval Plan — mantelpiece activation — is GO!

Dastardly tried to get us all distracted with the bookshelves while HE sneaked over to the mantelpiece! Classic misdirection! And Sneekly did the same thing earlier — tried to get everyone to stay in the Entrance Hall while HE came to the library first. These two are running the SAME playbook... but I'm sure it's just coincidence. Probably. Almost certainly.
